Registering and Signing In to Your Utility Billing Account

Start with the current bill, not memory. The account number, service address, and name formatting on the municipal record are the details registration is most likely to match. A previous owner's number, a landlord-controlled account, or an abbreviated street name can cause rejection even when the property is correct.

children.text: Use the bill as your source of truth
Open the municipal portal.
Use the city's official billing site from a desktop or mobile browser. Check the domain before entering account or payment details, especially if you are opening a saved bookmark or search result.
Choose Register if you are new to the service.
Enter the requested information exactly as it appears on the bill. Keep the legal account name, punctuation, spacing, and service-address formatting unchanged.
Verify the email address.
Registration usually requires an activation or verification message. Use an inbox you will continue to monitor, particularly when managing notices for a rental property or a portfolio.
Sign in with the new credentials.

After activation, confirm that the correct property, balance, bill history, and payment information appear. Save the official login page only after checking the address, and store the credentials in a password manager.

The municipal sign-in and EyeOnWater connection are separate steps. A successful billing login gives access to account records, but it does not by itself create consumption visibility. Keep the bill nearby for the later EyeOnWater setup, where the account details must match the municipal record.
Renters and new owners need to identify the account holder

A renter may be attempting to access an account still assigned to a landlord or former tenant. A buyer may also have an older bill while the city has created or reset the account after the ownership change. Repeatedly submitting outdated details rarely fixes either mismatch.

Check the latest bill and confirm who is responsible for the utility account. If responsibility has changed but registration still fails, contact Utility Billing instead of creating several accounts. Duplicate registrations can complicate payment records and billing-history checks.

Treat the first successful sign-in as a verification task. Confirm the service address, review the latest charge, and save the account number securely. For multi-family properties, note how the applicable tariff tier is displayed on the bill after login. That record is useful when portal fields do not match the property's tenancy or ownership paperwork.

exact bill credentials

Follow this sequence:
Confirm the municipal account:
Make sure the service address and account details are correct before opening EyeOnWater.
Create or open EyeOnWater:
Use the app or its associated web access and select the account-linking option.
Copy credentials exactly:
Avoid changing address abbreviations, spacing, account-number formatting, or the name associated with the bill.
Check the dashboard:
Look for meter readings or usage information after authorisation. A blank dashboard means the connection needs investigation, not that the municipal login failed.

For building operators, the value of this separation is practical. Billing answers “what was charged,” while consumption monitoring helps investigate unusual use, possible leaks, and resident questions. Broader background on
smart water systems
can help property teams understand why meter data is increasingly treated as an operational tool rather than a simple reading.

If EyeOnWater shows no information, recheck the credentials against the latest bill first. A formatting mismatch is a likely starting point. If the details are correct, the meter may not yet be commissioned or available in the system, which is a reason to contact the city rather than repeatedly reinstalling the app.

single-family, secondary-suite, and multi-family or commercial accounts
, and the city's published rate material records further increases in 2025 (

A resident should start by matching the account type to the property. A property manager should go further and compare the account category, base charge, metered-consumption band, billing period, and any balance carried forward. Those fields explain why two nearby properties can receive very different bills even when their apparent water use is similar.

For a multi-family property, don't assume the municipal account represents each suite individually. It may represent the property or a shared service, while internal allocation happens through a landlord, strata, or submetering arrangement. That distinction matters when residents ask why their personal consumption doesn't appear as a separate city charge.

Fixing Common Login Errors and Password Issues

A resident may enter the correct password and still fail to reach the bill. In practice, the problem is often a timed-out session, an outdated account number, or confusion between the municipal account and the separate EyeOnWater connection. Identify the symptom before changing browser settings or resetting credentials.

children.text: Match the fix to the failure
Forgotten password:

Use the portal's password-reset option and follow the email instructions promptly. Check spam if the message does not appear, and confirm that the email matches the municipal account. Registering again with another address can make ownership harder to verify.
Expired session:
A timed-out page may resemble a credential error. Open the official West Kelowna utility portal from its homepage and sign in again, rather than refreshing an old bill or payment page.
Multi-factor authentication issue:

If a code is required, confirm that the phone can receive messages or that the authenticator app is available. Managers sharing access with staff should not circulate one person's verification code. Update the approved contact method through the proper support process.
Browser problem:
Clear cached site data, allow required pop-ups, and try another supported browser. Private browsing can reveal a stored-session conflict, but it will not correct an invalid account number.
When the account number is rejected

An account number printed on an older bill may fail during a new registration after a property sale, tenant change, or municipal account reset. Compare the number and service address on the latest city-issued bill. If they still do not work together, stop submitting variations and preserve the details for support.

Record the email used, service address, latest bill date, and exact error message. Utility Billing can then check whether the account is active, whether contact details need updating, or whether another responsible party must claim it.

EyeOnWater requires separate troubleshooting. If the municipal login works but consumption is missing in the app, check the linkage credentials and whether meter data is available. Repeatedly resetting the municipal password will not repair a broken app connection. A successful municipal sign-in also does not guarantee that the EyeOnWater account has been linked correctly.
Contacting Utility Billing Support and Managing Account Changes

Self-service works well for routine bill viewing and payments. It's less suitable when responsibility has changed, an account number no longer matches, or a move requires a meter read. West Kelowna asks residents to contact Utility Billing
at least 24 hours before moving
so the account can be closed or opened and the meter read arranged (

Before calling the dedicated utility billing contact line, prepare:
Account information:
Account number and service address from the latest bill.
Occupancy details:
Move-in or move-out date, responsible party, and forwarding information.
Evidence of the problem:
Screenshot or exact wording of the portal error, without sharing your password.
Billing context:
Bill date, disputed line, payment date, and confirmation information if applicable.

Property managers should keep a separate record for each unit or building and coordinate account closures before handing over keys. That prevents a resident from inheriting unclear balances and preserves a clean history for the next account holder.

EyeOnWater serves a different purpose, providing consumption visibility after the account is linked with the correct credentials. Treating both services as one login can lead to repeated registration attempts and avoidable password resets.

A growing account base needs dependable access

The portal is an established service channel for households, landlords, strata councils, and property managers. Statistics Canada recorded 32,655 residents in 2016 and 36,078 in 2021, representing a 10.5% increase over five years (Statistics Canada census profile). The same 2021 profile lists 13,974 occupied private dwellings and a population density of 295.5 people per square kilometre, context for the households and accounts needing reliable billing access.

The city promoted e-bill delivery to more than 4,000 customers in 2025, and the portal remains active and updated in 2026. Residents use it to check balances, confirm payments, download bills, and manage account details during a tenancy or ownership change.

Practical rule: Create and verify the municipal account first. Then set up EyeOnWater separately for consumption data.

Owners and managers face a related record-matching problem when addresses, account numbers, and occupants change. The discussion of utility provider data integration is useful for reconciling those fields across a property portfolio. The bill remains the working reference when portal details do not match, especially for multi-family properties where tariff tiers may appear in the charges after login.

Registering and Signing In to Your Utility Billing Account

Start with the current bill, not memory. The account number, service address, and name formatting on the municipal record are the details registration is most likely to match. A previous owner's number, a landlord-controlled account, or an abbreviated street name can cause rejection even when the property is correct.

Use the bill as your source of truth

  1. Open the municipal portal. Use the city's official billing site from a desktop or mobile browser. Check the domain before entering account or payment details, especially if you are opening a saved bookmark or search result.

  2. Choose Register if you are new to the service. Enter the requested information exactly as it appears on the bill. Keep the legal account name, punctuation, spacing, and service-address formatting unchanged.

  3. Verify the email address. Registration usually requires an activation or verification message. Use an inbox you will continue to monitor, particularly when managing notices for a rental property or a portfolio.

  4. Sign in with the new credentials. After activation, confirm that the correct property, balance, bill history, and payment information appear. Save the official login page only after checking the address, and store the credentials in a password manager.

The municipal sign-in and EyeOnWater connection are separate steps. A successful billing login gives access to account records, but it does not by itself create consumption visibility. Keep the bill nearby for the later EyeOnWater setup, where the account details must match the municipal record.

Renters and new owners need to identify the account holder

A renter may be attempting to access an account still assigned to a landlord or former tenant. A buyer may also have an older bill while the city has created or reset the account after the ownership change. Repeatedly submitting outdated details rarely fixes either mismatch.

Check the latest bill and confirm who is responsible for the utility account. If responsibility has changed but registration still fails, contact Utility Billing instead of creating several accounts. Duplicate registrations can complicate payment records and billing-history checks.

Treat the first successful sign-in as a verification task. Confirm the service address, review the latest charge, and save the account number securely. For multi-family properties, note how the applicable tariff tier is displayed on the bill after login. That record is useful when portal fields do not match the property's tenancy or ownership paperwork.

Linking Your Account to EyeOnWater for Consumption Visibility

Municipal billing access doesn't automatically provide a complete water-use dashboard. West Kelowna's water-meter programme makes readings available through the EyeOnWater app only after you register and link the utility account, so the second step depends on the first.

Complete the connection in the right order

First, sign in to the West Kelowna municipal account and keep the bill available. Then open EyeOnWater and register or connect the water account using the exact bill credentials. The municipal login establishes access to city billing information, while EyeOnWater verifies the water-account identity for consumption data.

Follow this sequence:

  • Confirm the municipal account: Make sure the service address and account details are correct before opening EyeOnWater.
  • Create or open EyeOnWater: Use the app or its associated web access and select the account-linking option.
  • Copy credentials exactly: Avoid changing address abbreviations, spacing, account-number formatting, or the name associated with the bill.
  • Check the dashboard: Look for meter readings or usage information after authorisation. A blank dashboard means the connection needs investigation, not that the municipal login failed.

For building operators, the value of this separation is practical. Billing answers “what was charged,” while consumption monitoring helps investigate unusual use, possible leaks, and resident questions. Broader background on smart water systems can help property teams understand why meter data is increasingly treated as an operational tool rather than a simple reading.

If EyeOnWater shows no information, recheck the credentials against the latest bill first. A formatting mismatch is a likely starting point. If the details are correct, the meter may not yet be commissioned or available in the system, which is a reason to contact the city rather than repeatedly reinstalling the app.

Reading Your Bill and Understanding Multi-Family Tariff Tiers

Logging in is only useful if you can interpret the charges. West Kelowna publishes different quarterly water rates for single-family, secondary-suite, and multi-family or commercial accounts, and the city's published rate material records further increases in 2025 (West Kelowna water and sewer rate document).

A resident should start by matching the account type to the property. A property manager should go further and compare the account category, base charge, metered-consumption band, billing period, and any balance carried forward. Those fields explain why two nearby properties can receive very different bills even when their apparent water use is similar.

Compare the category before questioning the amount

Account Type Billing Frequency Rate Structure Common Use Case
Single-family Quarterly Applicable base charge plus metered consumption Detached home
Secondary suite Quarterly Category-specific base charge plus metered consumption Home with an approved or separately recognised suite
Multi-family or commercial Quarterly Category-specific base charge plus metered consumption bands Apartment, condominium, strata, or commercial property

The table reflects the city's published categories and quarterly structure. It isn't a substitute for checking the current bill or rate document, particularly because the city has changed rates. The important audit question is whether the account has been placed in the correct category.

For a multi-family property, don't assume the municipal account represents each suite individually. It may represent the property or a shared service, while internal allocation happens through a landlord, strata, or submetering arrangement. That distinction matters when residents ask why their personal consumption doesn't appear as a separate city charge.

A manager can use the portal to download or review the municipal bill, then compare it with internal meter records. Guidance on how to read a water meter is useful when consumption figures need to be checked against a physical or submeter reading.

Look for a category that doesn't match the building, a base charge that seems inconsistent with the account setup, or a consumption band that doesn't align with the meter data. Record the bill date, account number, service address, and disputed line before contacting Utility Billing. That gives the city a precise starting point.

Fixing Common Login Errors and Password Issues

A resident may enter the correct password and still fail to reach the bill. In practice, the problem is often a timed-out session, an outdated account number, or confusion between the municipal account and the separate EyeOnWater connection. Identify the symptom before changing browser settings or resetting credentials.

Match the fix to the failure

Forgotten password: Use the portal's password-reset option and follow the email instructions promptly. Check spam if the message does not appear, and confirm that the email matches the municipal account. Registering again with another address can make ownership harder to verify.

Expired session: A timed-out page may resemble a credential error. Open the official West Kelowna utility portal from its homepage and sign in again, rather than refreshing an old bill or payment page.

Multi-factor authentication issue: If a code is required, confirm that the phone can receive messages or that the authenticator app is available. Managers sharing access with staff should not circulate one person's verification code. Update the approved contact method through the proper support process.

Browser problem: Clear cached site data, allow required pop-ups, and try another supported browser. Private browsing can reveal a stored-session conflict, but it will not correct an invalid account number.

When the account number is rejected

An account number printed on an older bill may fail during a new registration after a property sale, tenant change, or municipal account reset. Compare the number and service address on the latest city-issued bill. If they still do not work together, stop submitting variations and preserve the details for support.

Record the email used, service address, latest bill date, and exact error message. Utility Billing can then check whether the account is active, whether contact details need updating, or whether another responsible party must claim it.

EyeOnWater requires separate troubleshooting. If the municipal login works but consumption is missing in the app, check the linkage credentials and whether meter data is available. Repeatedly resetting the municipal password will not repair a broken app connection. A successful municipal sign-in also does not guarantee that the EyeOnWater account has been linked correctly.

Contacting Utility Billing Support and Managing Account Changes

Self-service works well for routine bill viewing and payments. It's less suitable when responsibility has changed, an account number no longer matches, or a move requires a meter read. West Kelowna asks residents to contact Utility Billing at least 24 hours before moving so the account can be closed or opened and the meter read arranged (West Kelowna utility billing and rates).

Before calling the dedicated utility billing contact line, prepare:

  • Account information: Account number and service address from the latest bill.
  • Occupancy details: Move-in or move-out date, responsible party, and forwarding information.
  • Evidence of the problem: Screenshot or exact wording of the portal error, without sharing your password.
  • Billing context: Bill date, disputed line, payment date, and confirmation information if applicable.

Property managers should keep a separate record for each unit or building and coordinate account closures before handing over keys. That prevents a resident from inheriting unclear balances and preserves a clean history for the next account holder.
